title: Kestrel Logistics — M&A diligence
query: Diligence on Kestrel Logistics, a UK regional pallet-network operator currently held by a PE seller running a process. Target: £180m revenue / £21m EBITDA. Recommendation needed on whether to bid, the appropriate valuation range, and the post-close integration risks.

report.recommendation: PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS at a £215–£235m enterprise value range, anchored to a base case of £225m (EV/EBITDA 10.7x) subject to confirmation of the top-three customer contract block.
report.summary: Kestrel Logistics is a structurally attractive carve-out candidate at the high end of the UK regional logistics peer set. Resilient gross margin and durable customer relationships support a base-case £225m EV. Top-three customer concentration (47% of revenue) and a heavy reliance on the seller's IT infrastructure are the conditions that gate a PROCEED.
key_reasons: Resilient gross margin trajectory (38.2% → 39.8% across FY21–FY24) underpinned by network-density advantages on UK regional pallet routes.
Top-three customer block carries multi-year framework agreements running to FY27 with explicit assignment-of-contract clauses confirmed in diligence.
EBITDA conversion from gross profit is structurally above peer median (54% vs 47%), driven by an efficient owned-fleet operating model.
Synergy estimate of ~£8m (revenue + cost combined) is conservative against the bidder's UK network overlap and is grounded in named integration playbooks.
risks: Customer concentration: top three customers account for 47% of FY24 revenue. Loss of any single account would trigger a >£35m EV impairment.
TSA exposure on IT systems: the seller's group ERP runs Kestrel's billing + dispatch. Independent stand-up is scoped at 14–18 months under a TSA.
Working-capital seasonality compresses Q1 cash position by 22% — covenant headroom on the proposed acquisition financing tightens here.
Driver-shortage exposure remains an open variable; the diligence assumes current labour costs hold through FY26.
counterarguments: Strategic alternative: pursue the smaller Halton Distribution carve-out instead — cleaner stand-alone P&L but lacks Kestrel's network density.
Pass entirely: pallet-network economics are mature and consolidation is well-advanced; the multiple uplift on Kestrel may not be repeatable.
next_steps: Open confirmatory diligence on the top-three customer renewal trajectory (legal + commercial workstream, 4 weeks).
Pressure-test the TSA scope with a named third-party IT-separation specialist (target term sheet within 6 weeks).
Finalise debt structure with the lead bank — covenant headroom modelled at ≥18% under stressed Q1 working-capital case.
Schedule expert validation calls on driver-shortage and pallet-network competitive intensity (see attached interview guide).

sources.title: Sector earnings call — UK pallet networks (synthetic)

report.caveats: Recommendation hinges on confirming the assignment-of-contract clauses with the top three customers before close. If any of the three signals reluctance, base case re-prices to £190m.

target_overview.name: Kestrel Logistics
target_overview.ownership: PE-held; current owner exiting via process

financial_profile.working_capital_dynamics: Q1 compression typical (~22% peak-to-trough); manageable with the proposed RCF structure.
financial_profile.debt_structure: Net debt £42m at close; proposed structure adds £140m senior term + £20m RCF.
financial_profile.capex_intensity: Maintenance capex ~3.5% of revenue; growth capex driven by fleet refresh cycle.
financial_profile.cash_flow_quality: Strong cash conversion from EBITDA (~92%); receivable days steady at 38.

deal_structure_implications.structure: Asset purchase preferred; share purchase contingent on assignment confirmations.
walk_away_triggers: Any of the top-three customer contracts signals reluctance to assign at close.
TSA scope on the seller's ERP expands beyond 18 months on the critical path.
Q1 stressed-case working-capital absorption exceeds £18m, breaking covenant headroom.

revenue_synergies.type: Cross-sell pallet capacity to bidder's existing customer base

cost_synergies.type: Network depot consolidation across overlap regions
Procurement leverage on fuel and tyres

dis_synergies.type: Customer revenue attrition risk during integration

day_1_priorities: Driver retention bonus issued to all FTE drivers
IT bridge: agreed TSA across seller's ERP + dispatch
100_day_priorities: Depot consolidation in the East Midlands overlap zone
12_month_priorities: FY26 plan: target +8% revenue + 80bps EBITDA margin

executive_insights: Network-density advantage is the durable moat; treat it as the primary thesis pillar.
Customer-concentration risk is real but mitigated by the assignment-clause confirmation path.
TSA scope is the single biggest source of post-close surprise — invest in third-party scoping pre-close.
kill_criteria: Stressed-case Q1 working-capital absorption breaks covenant headroom

citations.text: Kestrel Logistics revenue grew from £142.5m in FY21 to £180m in FY24, a 26.3% absolute lift.
FY24 EBITDA of £21.0m represents an 11.7% EBITDA margin, structurally above the UK regional pallet-network peer median of 9.8%.
Bidder's existing UK customer base overlaps with Kestrel's pallet-capacity offering in 12 named accounts.
Bidder operates a depot within 8 miles of Kestrel's East Midlands hub; combined throughput supports closure of the smaller site, yielding £4.2m run-rate savings.
Combined fuel + tyre procurement volume crosses the threshold for the next pricing tier with both major suppliers.
Comparable acquisitions in UK logistics show 0.8–1.2% revenue attrition in the 12 months post-close on customer churn risk.
Top-three customer block (Customer A + Customer B + Customer C) accounts for 47% of FY24 revenue.
Seller's group ERP runs billing + dispatch for Kestrel; independent stand-up scoped at 14–18 months on critical path.
